name: System Runtime API Hijacking
description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way an operating system runs applications. Hijacking execution flow can be for the purposes of persistence since this hijacked execution may reoccur at later points in time. 


On Android, adversaries may overwrite the standard OS API library with a malicious alternative to hook into core functions to achieve persistence. By doing this, the adversary’s code will be executed every time the overwritten API function is called by an app on the infected device.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

strategies.name: Detection of System Runtime API Hijacking

analytics.name: Analytic 1800
analytics.guidance: Correlates (1) modification or replacement of system runtime libraries or API resolution paths, (2) repeated invocation of hijacked APIs across multiple applications, and (3) inconsistent or suppressed outputs from those APIs compared to expected OS-enforced behavior. The defender observes a causal chain where system-level API behavior is altered, resulting in multiple applications exhibiting consistent anomalies in sensor access, permission checks, or system state reporting.

tuning.description: Correlation window across multiple applications invoking affected APIs
Set of APIs monitored for integrity (e.g., location, telephony, permission checks)
Number of applications required to exhibit anomalous API behavior to trigger detection
Baseline of expected API return values or behavior patterns per device state

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: multiple applications invoking core system APIs (e.g., sensor, permission, telephony) with abnormal or inconsistent return values across apps within short interval

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: device integrity degradation + root detected or system partition modification affecting runtime libraries (e.g., /system/lib*, /vendor/lib*)

references.description: K. Lu. (n.d.). Deep Technical Analysis of the Spyware FlexiSpy for Android. Retrieved September 10, 2019.

software.name: Dvmap
software.description: [Dvmap](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0420) replaces `/system/bin/ip` with a malicious version. [Dvmap](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0420) can inject code by patching `libdmv.so` or `libandroid_runtime.so`, depending on the Android OS version. Both libraries are related to the Dalvik and ART runtime environments. The patched functions can only call `/system/bin/ip`, which was replaced with the malicious version.(Citation: SecureList DVMap June 2017)

references.description: R. Unuchek. (2017, June 8). Dvmap: the first Android malware with code injection. Retrieved December 10, 2019.

software.name: Zen
software.description: [Zen](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0494) can install itself on the system partition to achieve persistence. [Zen](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0494) can also replace `framework.jar`, which allows it to intercept and modify the behavior of the standard Android API.(Citation: Google Security Zen)

references.description: Siewierski, L. (2019, January 11). PHA Family Highlights: Zen and its cousins . Retrieved July 27, 2020.

mitigations.name: Attestation
mitigations.description: Device attestation could detect unauthorized operating system modifications.

mitigations.name: System Partition Integrity
mitigations.description: Android Verified Boot can detect unauthorized modifications made to the system partition, which could lead to execution flow hijacking.(Citation: Android-VerifiedBoot)

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
